items.passage: In his 1499 treatise The Judgment of Two Languages, Central Asian poet Alisher Navoi maintained that Chagatai Turkic, his native language, was a richer medium for poetry than Persian, then the region’s dominant literary language. ______ Navoi himself composed considerable verse in Persian, under the pen name Fani. But the overwhelming majority of his writing is in Turkic.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence says Navoi championed Turkic as a language for poetry. The blank sentence admits a fact that seems to cut against that: he also wrote poems in Persian. The next sentence turns back with “But”: most of his work is in Turkic. “Granted” introduces a point the writer concedes before returning to the main claim.

A.why_wrong: Arguing that Turkic suited poetry would not cause Navoi to write verse in Persian; the Persian poems are a point against the argument, not a result of it.

C.why_wrong: “Additionally” would present the Persian verse as one more point supporting Navoi’s case for Turkic, but writing in Persian seems to work against that case, which is why the next sentence begins with “But.”

D.why_wrong: Writing verse in Persian is not similar to arguing for Turkic; it is a concession that the following sentence answers.
